title: Problem 07
markdown:
### Problem
The figure at the right represents a uniform 3 by 4 grid of streets. Adolf will walk from $A$ to $B$ and Bertha will walk from $B$ to $A$, taking paths of minimum length, namely 7 blocks. They start at the same time and walk at the same constant speed. At each intersection where there are two options for the direction to take, one is chosen at random (each with probability 1/2). What is the probability that they meet along the way? (That "they meet" means that at some time they are both at the same place.)

![Figure for Jerry Heuer heuer-2012-p07](study/assets/asset-heuer-2012-p07-heuer-2012-p07.png)

### Solution (adapted from the official solution)
The probability is $\frac{37}{256}$.

![Figure for Jerry Heuer heuer-2012-p07-solution](study/assets/asset-heuer-2012-p07-solution-heuer-2012-p07-solution.png)

Since they walk at the same constant speed and the shortest path has length 7, they must meet halfway—that is, in the middle of their fourth block (at time $t = 3.5$ blocks).

After walking 3 blocks each:
- Adolf is at one of the four vertices $P_1, P_2, P_3, P_4$.
- Bertha is at one of the four vertices $Q_1, Q_2, Q_3, Q_4$.

The probabilities of Adolf reaching each $P_i$ after 3 steps from $A$:
- $P_1$: $(1/2)^3 = 1/8$
- $P_2$: $\binom{3}{1}(1/2)^3 = 3/8$
- $P_3$: $\binom{3}{2}(1/2)^3 = 3/8$
- $P_4$: $(1/2)^3 = 1/8$

By symmetry from $B$, Bertha's probabilities of reaching each $Q_j$ are identical: $(1/8, 3/8, 3/8, 1/8)$.

They meet on the connecting edge $P_i Q_j$ if Adolf traverses it toward $B$ and Bertha traverses it toward $A$:
- Meeting on $P_1 Q_1$: $(1/8)(1) \cdot (1/8)(1/2) = 1/128 = 2/256$
- Meeting on $P_2 Q_1$: $(3/8)(1/2) \cdot (1/8)(1/2) = 3/256$
- Meeting on $P_2 Q_2$: $(3/8)(1/2) \cdot (3/8)(1/2) = 9/256$
- Meeting on $P_3 Q_2$: $(3/8)(1/2) \cdot (3/8)(1/2) = 9/256$
- Meeting on $P_3 Q_3$: $(3/8)(1/2) \cdot (3/8)(1/2) = 9/256$
- Meeting on $P_4 Q_3$: $(1/8)(1/2) \cdot (3/8)(1/2) = 3/256$
- Meeting on $P_4 Q_4$: $(1/8)(1/2) \cdot (1/8)(1) = 1/128 = 2/256$

Summing all mutual meeting probabilities:

$$\frac{2 + 3 + 9 + 9 + 9 + 3 + 2}{256} = \frac{37}{256}.$$

### Conceptual Explanation
Because the total path length is 7 blocks, meetings occur exclusively on the 7 vertical and horizontal segments connecting the diagonal level-3 cut $\{P_1, P_2, P_3, P_4\}$ to $\{Q_1, Q_2, Q_3, Q_4\}$. Summing over all joint step probabilities gives $37/256$.

### Key Technique
Midpoint cut partitioning for simultaneous random walks on directed grids.
